prompt: Shuffle a copy of a card list reproducibly with Collections.shuffle and a seeded Random, leaving the original list untouched. Complete the shuffled method in the starter file.
explanation: Collections.shuffle rearranges a list in place, so to leave the caller's list untouched you must first make a defensive copy with new ArrayList<>(cards). Passing a seeded Random to shuffle makes the permutation reproducible: the same seed always produces the same order. This copy-then-mutate pattern is a common way to offer a 'pure' API on top of an in-place library method.
hints: Collections.shuffle modifies the list you give it -- so do not give it the original.
Make a copy first: java.util.List<String> copy = new java.util.ArrayList<>(cards);
Shuffle with Collections.shuffle(copy, new java.util.Random(seed)) and return copy.
